title: Gym owners: earn £500 per learner
summary: The PT Launch Lab Gym Partnership Programme turns your members, prospects and ex-members into qualified personal trainers - in your gym. You earn £500 for every learner who enrols through your link or QR code, paid upfront. No set-up fees, no monthly fees, no financial risk. We handle marketing, enrolment, education, support and delivery; you get better PTs on your floor, happier members and stronger retention. Book a 15-minute call - no pressure, just a strategic conversation about growth.

title: Start at Level 2: Gym Instructing
summary: You do not have to qualify as a personal trainer on day one. The NCFE Level 2 Certificate in Gym Instructing is the entry point - it gets you working on the gym floor, earning and building experience with real members, while you study towards your Level 3. Most employers will take a good Level 2 with the right attitude. Study online, at your own pace, from anywhere in the UK.

title: Level 3 Diploma in Personal Training
summary: The Level 3 is the qualification that makes you a personal trainer - programme design, nutrition, behaviour change, and the business side most courses skip. Ours is an NCFE diploma on the Ofqual register, delivered fully online with real tutor support. Built by gym owners who have hired over 500 trainers, so you learn what actually gets you employed, not just what gets you qualified.

title: Level 2 and Level 3 combined diploma
summary: Gym Instructing and Personal Training in one route. The Level 2 gets you on the gym floor and earning while you study; the Level 3 makes you a personal trainer. Taking them together is cheaper and faster than buying them separately, and you finish with the qualification employers actually ask for. Fully online, UK-wide, with tutors who answer.

title: Career change into personal training
summary: Most people who retrain as a PT are not 22 and fresh out of college. They are in their thirties, in a job they have outgrown, wondering whether it is too late. It is not. Study online around your current work, qualify with an Ofqual-regulated NCFE diploma, and leave the day job when the income is there - not before. We will be straight with you about what it takes and what it pays.

title: Ofqual regulated, NCFE accredited
summary: There are a lot of PT courses online and not all of them are worth the paper. Ours is an NCFE qualification on the Ofqual register, recognised by CIMSPA - which is what gyms and insurers actually check. If you are comparing providers, ask each of them for their awarding body and their Ofqual reference. If they cannot answer that quickly, it tells you what you need to know.

title: Payment plans available
summary: The qualification is an investment, so you do not have to pay for it in one go. Spread the cost across monthly instalments and start studying straight away - a deposit and a plan, no drawn-out finance application. Talk to us about which level fits you before you commit to anything.

title: What do personal trainers actually earn?
summary: Nobody in this industry wants to give you a straight answer on money, so here it is. Employed gym-floor PTs in the UK typically start low. Self-employed trainers with a full book earn considerably more, but they carry rent, insurance and the quiet months. The gap between the two is almost entirely business skill, not training knowledge. We break the real numbers down rather than quoting you a best case and hoping you do not check.

title: Work out your PT earnings before you commit
summary: Before you spend a penny on a qualification, it is worth knowing what the job actually pays. Our salary calculator lets you model client numbers, session rates and hours to see what you would realistically take home as a personal trainer - employed or self-employed. Free to use, no email required. Go in with your eyes open.

title: Am I too old to become a personal trainer?
summary: We get asked this most weeks, usually by someone in their late thirties or forties. The honest answer is no, and in a lot of cases age works in your favour. Your clients are far more likely to be 45 and deconditioned than 22 and competing. Someone who has lived a bit, held down a career and understands real constraints tends to keep clients longer than someone who has not.

title: Leaving the 9-5 for personal training
summary: The mistake is handing in your notice the day the certificate arrives. Qualify while you are still earning, build a handful of clients in evenings and weekends, and go full time when the numbers stack up. Less romantic, far more likely to work. We will help you plan the transition properly rather than cheerlead you off a cliff.

title: Going self-employed as a PT
summary: Self-employed trainers keep more of every session but carry everything else: gym rent, insurance, tax, pension, and the months when someone cancels. It can be a genuinely good living if you treat it as a business from day one. That means knowing your numbers, your rates and your client acquisition before you need them, not after.

title: Start your own personal training business
summary: Most PT courses stop at anatomy and programme design, then leave you to work out pricing, packaging, sales and retention on your own. That is the part that decides whether you are still training clients in two years. Our course includes the business side - how to get clients, what to charge, and how to keep people past month three.

title: Mentorship, not just a certificate
summary: Qualifying is the easy part. Knowing what to do in week three when a client stops replying, or how to price a block without undercutting yourself, is where most new trainers come unstuck. Every learner gets ongoing mentorship from people running real gyms - not a forum, not a PDF, actual answers from people doing the job.

title: Do UK gyms accept online PT qualifications?
summary: Yes - provided the qualification is regulated. Gyms and insurers care about the awarding body and the Ofqual listing, not whether you sat in a classroom. An NCFE Level 3 studied online carries the same recognition as one studied in person. What is not accepted is an unregulated certificate from a provider with no awarding body, and there are plenty of those about.

title: Retraining as a personal trainer
summary: Coming from hospitality, retail, the forces, teaching or an office job? Every one of those gives you something the average newly qualified trainer lacks - dealing with people, handling pressure, showing up when you do not feel like it. The training knowledge is teachable. That part is not. Study online around the job you have now.

title: Fast-track your PT qualification
summary: If you have the time to give it, you do not have to spread the course over a year. The fast-track route condenses the same NCFE Level 3 content into a tighter schedule so you can qualify and start earning sooner. Same qualification, same regulation, less waiting. It suits people between jobs or with a clear runway - we will tell you honestly if it does not suit you.

title: Study around shifts and family
summary: Our learners are nurses, warehouse staff, parents and people on rotating shifts. The course is built for that - no fixed lecture times, no travelling to a campus, everything accessible whenever you get an hour. Tutor support runs alongside it, so studying flexibly does not mean studying alone.

title: See what our graduates are doing now
summary: The fairest way to judge a course is to look at where people end up. Our graduates are working commercial gym floors, running independent studios, coaching online and building client books from scratch. Real names, real gyms, real outcomes - have a read before you choose any provider, including us.

title: Not sure which course is right?
summary: Level 2, Level 3, or both together - the right answer depends on whether you are already working in a gym, how quickly you need to earn, and what you want to be doing in two years. Our career planner walks you through it in a few minutes, or you can just call us and we will tell you straight. We would rather point you at the right course than sell you the expensive one.
